sentences.show: In 1971, a man hijacked a plane, took $200,000, and jumped out into the night. Nobody ever found him.
The day before Thanksgiving, he paid cash for a ticket from Portland to Seattle, as "Dan Cooper".
Dark suit, black tie, raincoat. He ordered a bourbon, and handed a stewardess a note.
She thought it was his phone number, and dropped it in her purse.
He leaned over. "Miss, you'd better look at that note. I have a bomb."
His briefcase was full of wires and red cylinders. He wanted $200,000, and four parachutes.
In Seattle, he swapped the passengers for the money, and ordered the plane back into the air.
Slow, low, with the rear stairs open. Two fighter jets followed, out of sight.
At about 8 p.m., a warning light came on. The stairs were down.
When the plane landed in Reno, he was gone. Somewhere over the forests of Washington, he had jumped.
The FBI searched for years. They found nothing. Not a body, not a parachute.
Then, in 1980, an eight-year-old boy was building a campfire on the banks of the Columbia River.
In the sand, he found rotting bundles of $20 bills. The serial numbers matched.
The rest of the money has never been found. Neither has the man.
It is still the only unsolved hijacking in American aviation. So who was D. B. Cooper?
Cooper vanished into the night. Don't vanish on us. Subscribe.
